phrases: Ask an AI for a source,
and it might give you one that doesn't exist.
Title, author, even page numbers.
It isn't lying.
It's doing what it was built to do.
Here's why AI sometimes makes things up.
A language model writes by predicting the next token,
using patterns learned from huge amounts of text.
Facts that appeared again and again leave strong patterns,
so those answers are usually right.
But rare facts, like a small study or an obscure date, leave weak patterns.
The model still has to write something,
so it writes what a right answer would sound like.
Researchers call this a hallucination.
And many tests used to train and rank AI
reward a confident guess over "I'm not sure."
Tools that search the web or your documents first can help.
But no AI is right every time.
So use AI for ideas and drafts.
For facts that matter, check the source,
and make sure it's real.
